title: Adaptive client-side token pacing harness for large-scale SSE/WebSocket chat streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a load testing harness that emulates realistic client-side streaming behavior for SSE and WebSocket chat/completions, focusing on token-level pacing and p95 token emission latency. The harness should exercise prefix/KV cache hot/cold paths, simulate network jitter and client backpressure, and produce stable metrics (tokens/sec, p95, error-rate, reconnects) usable for automated regression detection and capacity planning.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run O(100k) concurrent simulated client sessions across multiple generator workers and report aggregated tokens/sec and p95 token-emission latency
Support both SSE and WebSocket with ability to flip protocol mid-run to exercise fallback logic
Client-emitted token pacing options: fixed-rate, adaptive (based on server ACKs), bursty (Poisson), and KV-cache-aware prefix reuse
Integration with telemetry pipeline: DataDog metrics and trace spans with tags: model, region, protocol, cohort
Automated regression detection: baseline comparisons with configurable p95 and tokens/sec thresholds and a simple bisect trigger that opens a GitHub issue template when thresholds breach
Synthetic session scripts that include long-tail conversations (>2048 tokens) and short QPS bursts to validate kernel scheduling and KV cache eviction behaviour
tasks: Design harness architecture and worker orchestration (stateless generator workers + central coordinator)
Implement client simulator with token-level emit control and pluggable pacing strategies
Add KV-cache-awareness: simulate warm, lukewarm, and cold prefixes with configurable reuse ratios
Develop jitter and packet-loss emulation layer (client-side latency distribution, TCP-level retry patterns)
Wire metrics: tokens/sec, token-p95, stream-attach-latency, reconnects, error-codes to telemetry
Create regression detector comparator and GitHub issue auto-template for detected regressions
Build dashboards in DataDog: cohort-level p95, tokens/sec, and model-variant breakdown
E2E runbook and cost-estimate for running a full 24-hour stress sweep
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff - aligned with SRE (Marta Ruiz) and Runtime team on goals. Decided to prioritize client-side pacing to surface queueing/backpressure behaviours not visible in server-only harnesses.

2026-02-18: Prototype - first generator worker can spawn 1k WS sessions with fixed-rate pacing. Observed skew in token emission p95 due to TCP slow-start when simulating many new clients; flagged network emulation improvements.

2026-02-25: Design decision - implement KV-cache-aware mode: sessions will tag prefixes as warm/lukewarm/cold with configurable ratios. Tradeoff: increases workload complexity but exposes real-world cache miss amplification seen in production.
2026-03-03: Review feedback from Runtime (Sanjay Verma) - suggested lightweight kernel scheduling probe (short long-run sequences) to capture kernel-selection regressions; added to tasks.
2026-03-08: Telemetry integration - pushed metrics schema and draft DataDog dashboards (DD link below). Need team to review tag names for downstream billing pipelines.

2026-03-12: Regression detection prototype - comparator computes historical baseline using last 7 days median and flags >15% p95 regression or >20% tokens/sec drop. Auto-issue template wired to GitHub but needs permission gating for write access.
Blocked: running large-scale cross-region experiments until Dedicated pool quota increases (ticket ENG-41210). Coordinating with Capacity team.
Next: finalize burst-mode Poisson pacing and integrate SSE fallback switcher for mid-run protocol flip tests.
